title: What Did Fastly Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
detail:
What Did Fastly Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
Trefis Team

FSLY
^GSPC
NET
AKAM
ZS
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Fastly (FSLY) stock returned 241.5% in the twelve months to October 9, 2026, easily outpacing the 17.0% gain for the S&P 500. Buyers appear to have been paying for a clear shift in the underlying business: sales began growing faster again, and losses shrank. Investors stepping in today are betting that this momentum will hold, while observers who missed the rally might wonder if the company offered advance warning. How early did Fastly show that its sales were turning?

Fastly Gave A First Sign In February 2025

The initial signal arrived on February 12, 2025, about eight months before the run began. During a quarterly earnings call, management outlined a new approach to how Fastly sells its products. The strategy involved pitching customers on the company's entire range, including security solutions and bot protection.

Management noted on that call that demand had weakened at a few of its largest customers. Revenue from clients outside its ten largest accounts, however, grew 16% year over year. Because total revenue grew only 2.0% in the fourth quarter of 2024, the health of those smaller accounts remained masked in the overall figures. Anyone buying the stock after that presentation was investing in a turnaround plan, not yet a proven result.

Fastly's Next Two Filings Backed The Plan

That strategy started taking shape across the subsequent two quarterly reports, both filed before the stock run. Fastly filed its results on May 7, 2025, showing revenue grew 8.2% in the quarter ended March 2025. Top-line growth then reached 12.3% in the second quarter of 2025, detailed in a report filed on August 6, 2025.

Some investors noticed the initial acceleration immediately. Fastly stock was up about 30% for the week by early Friday, according to a news report on May 9, 2025. The company's regulatory filings showed faster sales by August 6, 2025, two months before the twelve-month window that produced the 241.5% gain began.

Neither filing demonstrated a profit. Fastly's operating loss was still 24.6% of revenue in the second quarter of 2025. Anyone waiting for proof that revenue growth would translate into profit did not have it yet.

Are Fastly's Sales Still Picking Up?

Sales momentum continued through the latest reported quarter. Management announced on the August 5, 2026 call that revenue grew 23% to $183.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. Security revenue grew 43%, aligning with the strategy detailed in February 2025. The company's operating loss over the past twelve months narrowed to 12.0% of revenue, down from 24% a year earlier. Fastly's overall stock run was substantially larger than that of its peer Cloudflare, which returned 64.1% over the same twelve months.

Why Are We Positive on ATI?

With its materials flying in nearly every commercial and military aircraft in service today, ATI (NYSE:ATI) produces highly specialized materials and components for aerospace, defense, medical, and energy applications using advanced metallurgy and manufacturing processes.

1. Skyrocketing Revenue Shows Strong Momentum

A company's long-term sales performance can indicate its overall quality. Any business can put up a good quarter or two, but the best consistently grow over the long haul. Luckily, ATI's sales grew at an excellent 12.9% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years. Its growth beat the average industrials company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.

2. Outstanding Long-Term EPS Growth

Analyzing the long-term change in earnings per share (EPS) shows whether a company's incremental sales were profitable — for example, revenue could be inflated through excessive spending on advertising and promotions.

ATI's full-year EPS flipped from negative to positive over the last five years. This is a good sign and shows it's at an inflection point.

3. Increasing Free Cash Flow Margin Juices Financials

Free cash flow isn't a prominently featured metric in company financials and earnings releases, but we think it's telling because it accounts for all operating and capital expenses, making it tough to manipulate. Cash is king.

As you can see below, ATI's margin expanded by 18.8 percentage points over the last five years. The company's improvement shows it's heading in the right direction, and we can see it became a less capital-intensive business because its free cash flow profitability rose more than its operating profitability. title: Why Every Snap Investor Is Looking At This One Number
detail:
Why Every Snap Investor Is Looking At This One Number

META

PINS
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Investors buying Snap (SNAP) stock may be betting on a surprising part of the business: the subscriptions it sells directly to users. Most people still consider Snap an advertising company, but a growing portion of its revenue now comes straight from its audience. The stock lost 28% over the past twelve months, contrasting with a 17.0% return for the S&P 500. So, how many of Snapchat's users actually pay for it?

Less Than 3% Of Snap's Monthly Users Pay

Snapchat had 971 million monthly active users in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. Less than 3% of them were paying subscribers. Executives provided both figures on the company's August earnings call.

Subscriptions lead a business segment that already generates real money. Snap's revenue outside advertising grew 85% to $316 million in the quarter. Executives said Snapchat+, Memory Storage, and the Lens+ subscription led that growth.

Advertising is still the dominant business, but its expansion is much slower. Ad revenue rose 9% to $1.28 billion in the same quarter. So revenue outside advertising accounted for about a fifth of Snap's $1.6 billion total, making it the faster-growing side of the company.

Is Snap Getting Closer To A Profit?

The figures of the past three years suggest it is, although Snap still loses money. Its net loss was 4.9% of revenue over the last twelve months, compared with a 13.3% profit margin for the S&P 500. That loss remains a central concern for investors.

The loss has shrunk every year. It was 30% of revenue three years ago and 24% two years ago, before narrowing to 9.7% a year ago. Snap is also already bringing in cash. Executives noted the company has generated positive free cash flow for eight consecutive quarters.

Management expects the financial improvement to continue. On the August call, executives said the company expects sustained positive net income beginning in 2027. They also expect the money users pay directly to keep growing materially faster than the business as a whole.

There is room for expansion. Management said app subscription penetration seems to be typically around 7% to 12% over the long term, well above Snapchat's share today. This range was offered as a comparison, not a forecast for Snapchat itself.

Snap cannot rely on subscriptions alone yet, and its expenses are rising. The company raised its forecast for full-year infrastructure costs to $1.65 billion to $1.70 billion, up from $1.60 billion to $1.65 billion previously.
